key_insight: SurgFormer is a multiresolution gated transformer that learns solver-quality soft-tissue deformation on volumetric meshes, enabling near real-time, nodewise displacement prediction and explicit support for resections.
problem_solved: High‑fidelity biomechanical simulators are too slow for interactive surgical applications and struggle to scale; SurgFormer replaces costly solvers with a data‑driven model that scales to large meshes and handles tissue cutting/resection.
method: Build a fixed multiresolution mesh hierarchy and process geometry at multiple scales.
Stack multibranch blocks that fuse local message passing, coarse global self‑attention, and pointwise feedforward updates.
Train on solver‑generated displacement fields so the model predicts nodewise deformations (including resections) at near real‑time speed.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a scalable, fast surrogate for biomechanical simulation suitable for interactive surgical systems, data augmentation, and downstream learning tasks—cutting computational cost while retaining solver-like fidelity.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: mesh hierarchy (fine→coarse) with multibranch block showing local message passing + global attention + feedforward fusion.
Before/after mesh overlay: ground‑truth solver displacements vs SurgFormer predictions (color-coded nodewise error).
Speed vs accuracy plot: solver vs SurgFormer (latency on x, error on y) to highlight real‑time advantage.
Illustration showing resection/cutting and the model updating mesh displacements in real time.
paper_title: SurgFormer: Scalable Learning of Organ Deformation with Resection Support and Real-Time Inference
paper_authors: Ashkan Shahbazi, Elaheh Akbari, Kyvia Pereira, Jon S. Heiselman, Annie C. Benson
